name: Nha Trang
summary: A coastal city in south-central Vietnam that hosted major U.S. military facilities during the war. Larry remembers spending approximately his first two months in Vietnam here, from around September 1964 — a period when, in his words, "they didn't know where to put us" — with Ron Tototz and Parr. The beach photographs VN-0021 and VN-0022 belong to beach hut #3 or #4, run by two girls selling soda pop, beer, and shrimp — three large shrimp for 25 cents. Larry also attaches a loss to this beach: a medic from Nebraska went out into the water and disappeared. On 2026-09-12 he called it "the most beautiful place you ever saw" (VN-0018).
researchNotes: Which unit or facility Larry was attached to at Nha Trang has not been identified — his own 'they didn't know where to put us' suggests a replacement/holding status rather than a unit posting, which would explain the difficulty. The drowned Nebraska medic is a findable casualty record (unresolved question #14). The coordinates mark the city itself; Larry's specific location within it is unknown. 2026-09-12 (giscus-vn-0018-c18415793, -c18415813): the girl in VN-0018 "is one of the girls that was selling shrimp. You could get a shrimp 6 - 7 niches long and a beer for 25 cents. Average pay of a Vietnamese was 10 cents a day." The price agrees with his 2026-08-15 figure for the beach huts (three large shrimp for 25 cents) while describing a different purchase; both are kept as given.
